item.title: Polynomial Invariants of Pseudo-Anosov Maps (Addendum)
item.description: arXiv:2610.28959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that homology, puncture, and symplectic polynomials of a pseudo-Anosov map arXiv:1001.5094 are invariants of the mapping class, as well as of the conjugacy class.
item.dc:creator: Merrick Dodge, Keiko Kawamuro

item.title: Asymptotics of Masur-Veech volume of strata of quadratic differentials with many simple poles
item.description: arXiv:2610.28963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide large $n$ asymptotics of the Masur-Veech volumes for strata of quadratic differentials of the form $\mathcal{Q}_g(n,d_1,\dots,d_k,-1^{n+D-4g+4})$, where all positive integers $d_i$ are fixed and $D=d_1+\dots+d_k$. Our formulae are particularly explicit in genus $1$. For the two series of non-varying strata $\mathcal{Q}_1(n,-1^n)$ and $\mathcal{Q}_1(n,1,-1^{n+1})$ we give simple closed formulae for the volumes for any $n$.
item.dc:creator: Kasra Rafi, Anton Zorich

item.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.28986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi (k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. The second story starts from the poset of $k$-shuffle partitions, which were introduced by Drew Armstrong and explored in depth in his thesis arXiv:math/0611106. In this paper, we focus on the combinatorial aspects of $k$-shuffle braid groups starting from the poset of $k$-shuffle non-crossing partitions. We build a CW-complex on which the groups act freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly, which we show is CAT(0) for dimension up to 7. For higher dimension, we show that the CAT(0) property is implied by the conjecture of Brady and McCammond that the dual braid complex is CAT(0) (arXiv:0909.4778).
item.dc:creator: Chlo\'e Postel-Vinay

item.title: Affine $G$-multibiquandle modules for colored links I: representability of coloring functors and color-profile polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.29011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, let $G$ be an abelian group, and fix $u\in R[G]^\times$. For each component-labeled oriented link diagram $(D,\sigma)$, we construct a finitely presented $R[G]$-module $M_u(D,\sigma;R[G])$ with a universal affine coloring $U_{D,\sigma}$. Every affine coloring with values in an $R[G]$-module factors uniquely through $U_{D,\sigma}$ by a module homomorphism. Thus the module represents the affine coloring functor. Each specified colored Reidemeister move induces a unique module isomorphism compatible with coloring transport, and the module isomorphism class is a colored-link invariant. The representing modules and universal colorings commute with arbitrary scalar extension, without a flatness assumption. For classical links, simultaneous rescaling of the component labels removes the common deformation unit. For any multibiquandle, associated-biquandle colorings decompose into fibers indexed by component labelings. For finite targets and palettes, we define a color-profile polynomial recording the joint distribution of fiber sizes and numbers of palette labels used, and prove its invariance under oriented link isotopy. In the affine case, the representing modules determine these fibers, and their specialized dimensions determine the coloring counts over finite fields. The color-profile polynomial is not determined, in general, by the full unweighted distribution of coloring-fiber sizes. It therefore retains information beyond the associated-biquandle coloring count.
item.dc:creator: Sang Youl Lee

item.title: On discrete symmetries of the cube of smoothings
item.description: arXiv:2511.01446v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A link diagram with a labeled barycentric subdivision endows the cube of resolutions with an additional combinatorial structure. We study the set of symmetries, preserving this structure. We construct a combinatorial link invariant, based on the symmetries of triangulated smoothings.
item.dc:creator: Eva Horvat

item.title: A Dehornoy-Type Ordering on Bridge Positions of Links
item.description: arXiv:2604.07790v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By a theorem of Hovland, bridge isotopy classes of $n$-bridge positions of links in $S^3$ correspond bijectively to Hilden double cosets $P_{2n}=H_{2n}\backslash B_{2n}/H_{2n}$. We use this correspondence to introduce Dehornoy-type orderings on bridge positions. After fixing a proper complexity function on $B_{2n}$, we assign to each double coset its Dehornoy-minimal braid among the elements of minimal complexity. Comparing these representatives by the Dehornoy order gives a strict total order $\prec_{D,n}$, and comparing them first by complexity and then by the Dehornoy order gives a strict well-order $\triangleleft_{D,n}$. For a link type $L$ and $n\geq b(L)$, we single out a canonical $n$-bridge position $\operatorname{CanPlat}_D^{(n)}(L)$: it is the $\triangleleft_{D,n}$-least element of the set of $n$-bridge positions of $L$, and the $\prec_{D,n}$-least element among those of minimal complexity, and its canonical braid coincides with the globally Dehornoy-minimal braid of minimal complexity representing $L$. We show by an example that, in general, it need not be least for $\prec_{D,n}$ on the whole set. Finally, we show that the fixed-level bridge finiteness conjecture is equivalent to boundedness of the complexities of the canonical representatives, and to the existence of a $\triangleleft_{D,n}$-greatest $n$-bridge position.
item.dc:creator: Makoto Ozawa

item.title: Global shadow estimates and Hausdorff measure criteria in higher rank
item.description: arXiv:2606.19779v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Patterson--Sullivan measures encode the distribution of orbits of discrete group actions near the boundary. We prove a global shadow lemma for Patterson--Sullivan measures associated to relatively Morse subgroups of higher-rank semisimple Lie groups. The estimate is uniform for shadows centered at arbitrary points in a Gromov model, including points deep in the cuspidal part, and expresses the contribution of each cusp in terms of peripheral growth. This extends the global shadow lemma of Stratmann--Velani for geometrically finite real hyperbolic groups. As applications, we establish local doubling and reverse doubling. Under Zariski density, we give necessary and sufficient criteria for Patterson--Sullivan measures to agree with the associated Hausdorff measures and to be Ahlfors regular. For symmetric linear forms, these criteria hold without Zariski density. We verify the criteria explicitly for cusped Hitchin representations and real-hyperbolic self-joinings.
item.dc:creator: Dongryul M. Kim, Hee Oh

item.title: Non-kinetic homotopy coherent actions on four-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.24548v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give the first example of a non-kinetic smooth homotopy coherent action of order two on a closed simply connected smooth four-manifold. This action is obtained by restricting a nontrivial smooth homotopy coherent action of the discrete circle group on a stabilized $K3$ surface. We also construct relatively non-kinetic smooth homotopy coherent extensions of boundary involutions over compact smooth $4$-manifolds. In addition, we exhibit boundary involutions that admit locally linear topological extensions but no smooth extensions over the same stabilized fillings. Nevertheless, we prove a Wall-type theorem showing that every free involution on a disjoint union of integral homology spheres extends smoothly over any simply connected smooth filling after sufficiently many stabilizations by $S^2\times S^2$.
item.dc:creator: Sungkyung Kang, JungHwan Park, Masaki Taniguchi

item.title: U torsion structure in Heegaard Floer homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.27646v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct infinite families of Brieskorn spheres with three singular fibers for which the difference between the largest and the second largest length of $U$-torsion in their Heegaard Floer homology $HF^-$ increases to infinity as the family parameter increases. In particular, these families give a negative answer to the strong geography restriction problem by Alfieri and Binns \cite[Question 1.10]{AB24} which was added to the recent K3 list \cite[Problem 3.55, Remark(5)]{K3}. As a consequence of the results by Alfieri and Binns, these families give the examples of integer homology spheres that are neither surgery on a knot nor large surgery on links.
item.dc:creator: Yuhui Chen, Shunyu Wan

item.title: Spherical growth of reciprocal classes in the Hecke Groups
item.description: arXiv:2411.00739v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma_p$ denote the Hecke group where $p=2r$, $r>0$. Let $\mathcal{N}_l$ denote the set of conjugacy classes of reciprocal elements of word length $l$ in $\Gamma_p$. We prove that for $l \to \infty$, $$|\mathcal{N}_l| = \mathcal{O}\left(\left\lfloor \tfrac{l+1}{2} \right\rfloor^{s-1} \rho^{\left\lfloor \tfrac{l+1}{2} \right\rfloor} \right), $$ where $\mathcal O$ is the `big O', $\rho \in [\sqrt{2}, 2]$ is the unique positive real root of $$ p(x) = x^{r+1} - 2\sum_{j=1}^{r-1} x^{r-j} - 1, $$ and $s$ is the maximal multiplicity among the roots of $p(x)$. Our method relies on the free product structure of the Hecke group $\Gamma_p$, a combinatorial counting function, and recurrence relations derived from cyclically reduced representatives. We also derive that the growth rate of the primitive reciprocal classes of word length $l$ is in agreement with that of $\mathcal{N}_l$. This work generalizes previous results for odd $p$ and provides an explicit asymptotic bound for all Hecke groups.
item.dc:creator: Debattam Das, Krishnendu Gongopadhyay

item.title: Semisimplicity of conformal blocks
item.description: arXiv:2507.06318v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that braid group representations associated to braided fusion categories and mapping class group representations associated to modular fusion categories are always semisimple. The proof relies on the theory of extensions in non-Abelian Hodge theory and on Ocneanu rigidity. By combining this with previous results on the existence of variations in Hodge structures, we further show that such a braid group or mapping class group representation preserves a non-degenerate Hermitian form and can be defined over some CM number field.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal f\"ur die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelles Journal), 2026
item.dc:creator: Pierre Godfard

item.title: Cobordism, spin structures, and profinite completions
item.description: arXiv:2601.05706v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth closed connected aspherical manifolds with good (in the sense of Serre) fundamental groups $G$ and $H$. We show that if $\widehat G\cong \widehat H$, then $M$ and $N$ are cobordant and the signatures of $M$ and $N$ agree modulo $8$. Moreover, $M$ is spin (resp. spin$^\mathbb{C}$) if and only if $N$ is spin (resp. spin$^\mathbb{C}$). We consider some analogous results for compact connected aspherical manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Sam Hughes, Andrew Ng

item.title: Regularity of Manhattan manifolds and exact dimensionality for relatively Anosov groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.13730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish several results about Patterson--Sullivan measures for relatively Anosov groups. First, we prove that these measures are exact dimensional with respect to visual metrics induced by Gromov models in the Groves--Manning quasi-isometry class. Under the additional assumption that the group is relatively Morse, we show that the associated scalar Cartan metric is Gromov hyperbolic and that the corresponding boundary premetric is a visual metric to which the exact-dimensionality theorem applies. Second, we prove that their Manhattan manifolds are $C^1$-regular, from which we deduce that the growth indicator is $C^1$-regular and strictly concave on the interior of the limit cone. This extends the case of Anosov representations by Kim--Oh--Wang. Our methods are dynamical, and we exploit the fact due to Kim--Oh and Blayac--Canary--Zhu--Zimmer that Bowen--Margulis--Sullivan measures for relatively Anosov groups are finite and mixing.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Reyes, Tianqi Wang

item.title: Self measurable embeddings of mapping class groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.12054v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a finite-type orientable surface without boundary, outside of a few low-complexity surfaces, we show that any measurable embedding of the associated mapping class group into itself is a measure equivalence. This is a measure-theoretic analog to the result of Ivanov and McCarthy that mapping class groups are co-Hopfian.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Gurieva
